lines.text: In most plants, the gauges, valves and warning lights aren't connected to anything.
So every shift, someone walks the floor with a clipboard.
So a pressure past its limit, or a slow leak, gets noticed hours too late.
Putting a sensor on every gauge costs thousands of dollars per point.
A patrol robot costs a hundred thousand.
Today's AI cameras spot people and pets, but judging danger needs a GPU-class model.
At the same time, another problem is growing.
In Taiwan, over seven hundred thousand older people now live alone.
As hearing and memory fade, pots are left burning on the stove, and smoke alarms go unheard.
Caregivers can't watch a camera all day, so by the time anyone notices, it's often too late.
So we built PatrolEye to check where danger starts, and warn you in words.
lines.say: So we built Patrol Eye to check where danger starts, and warn you in words.

lines.text: This is our working prototype: a camera on two motors, and a small computer that decides where to look.
It comes in two editions: for plants, with a depth camera, and for homes, with a webcam.
Now put it in a pump room.
Every hour, it walks the round for you: twenty-two gauges, valves and lights, from one spot on the wall.
When a pressure creeps past its limit, it zooms in, reads the dial, and warns the shift lead.
To test it for real, we built a pump room out of three screens, and broke things while it patrolled.
This is the plant edition's control room: here you see every reading and alert, as text, and every fault it caught.
At home, PatrolEye makes the rounds for her caregiver: is she up and about? Is the stove off?
lines.say: At home, Patrol Eye makes the rounds for her caregiver. Is she up and about? Is the stove off?

lines.text: If it finds her on the floor, the caregiver gets an alert right away.
On every round, it checks each spot and reports to the app. Open a report, and the clip shows the stove really is off.
The prototype runs on a Raspberry Pi 5, with an ASUS UGen300 M.2 module and its Hailo-10H chip.
lines.say: The prototype runs on a Raspberry Pi five, with an Asus U Gen three hundred M dot two module, and its Hailo ten H chip.

lines.text: For real deployment, we keep the same AI module, shrink everything around it, and mount it on the ceiling, where one unit sees the whole room, floor included.
Forty TOPS and eight gigabytes run a vision-language model, offline.
lines.say: Forty tops, and eight gigabytes, run a vision language model, offline.

lines.text: No live stream: just reports, and a clip you can open.
One camera that catches danger early, so nobody has to watch.
PatrolEye.
Private at home. Confidential at work.

opening.text: An AI camera that spots danger early.
